newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares up slightly, seen staying flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares up slightly, seen staying flat.

text.p: Polish shares on Monday rose slightly for the third session running and analysts said the market should stay flat this week amid selective buying before Bank Handlowy's large public offering starting in late May.

Analysts said some investors were already saving up for the $1-billion offering of Poland's largest commercial bank but that Monday gains by some larger firms suggested that some institutional investors were still making selective buys.
"For portfolio investors...if in the short-term it's a weak market then that's a good time to buy," said Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.
Large-cap Bank Slaski and industrial and trading firm Elektrim on Monday rebounded after recent falls and cement maker Gorazdze gained 5.8 percent after reporting good April earnings.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.6 percent to 16,474.2 and turnover fell 31.8 percent to 132.7 million zlotys ($42.1 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 39 to 38 with 21 stocks flat.
Analysts said more stocks could move sharply on Tuesday as most firms release April earnings data later on Monday.
They said banks could continue their earnings slump. BWR and PBR fell 5.6 and 4.3 respectively on Monday after publishing weak April earnings.
Builder Espebepe surged 9.6 percent the session after creditors accepted the company's version of a debt-relief deal envisaging an 80-percent write-off, analysts said.
The stock did not trade after price fixing due to excess demand, signalling another jump on Tuesday, analysts said.
